title: CTR-Sink: Attention Sink for Language Models in Click-Through Rate Prediction

problem.claim: CTR prediction estimates user click likelihood from historical behavioral data, and LM-based modeling of behavior sequences is increasingly used for this task.

gap.claim: Behavior sequences contain discrete actions separated by semantically empty tokens, unlike coherent natural language, causing fragmented attention and degraded prediction performance.

contributions.claim: CTR-Sink introduces behavior-level attention sinks tailored to recommendation scenarios.
The framework inserts sink tokens between consecutive behaviors and incorporates recommendation-specific signals such as temporal distance to create stable attention sinks.
It uses two-stage training to guide attention toward sink tokens and an attention-sink mechanism to amplify inter-sink dependencies for behavioral correlations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CTR-Sink as a novel framework introducing behavior-level attention sinks for recommendation scenarios.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on one industrial dataset and two open-source datasets, MovieLens and Kuairec, with visualization results validating effectiveness across scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: CTR prediction is a core recommendation task, and LM-based modeling of behavior sequences has gained traction.
The discrete, semantically sparse structure of behavior sequences differs from LM pre-training text and fragments attention.
CTR-Sink introduces behavior-level attention sinks using sink tokens, recommendation-specific signals, and attention-guiding training mechanisms.
The authors report evaluation across one industrial and two open-source datasets, plus visualizations.

source_observation.claim: When structured behavioral events are represented as text, semantically empty separators may disrupt attention to event boundaries and relationships.

interpretation.claim: Explicit intermediate tokens or mechanisms may help language models organize attention around meaningful behavioral units.

application.claim: For sequence-to-prediction systems built from discrete events, consider adding domain-specific boundary representations and training signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that attention sinks improve every event-sequence task or dataset.

unknowns: Quantitative performance results and statistical significance are not reported.
Baseline methods, ablations, and implementation details are not specified.
The industrial dataset, evaluation protocol, and visualization methodology are not described.
